'''Polina Solomonovna Landa''' ({{Langx|ru|Полина Соломоновна Ланда}}; February 15, 1931 – September 21, 2022) was a Soviet physicist.

==Early life and education==
Landa was born in [[Kyiv]], the daughter of Solomon V. Landa. Her family was Jewish. She graduated from high school in [[Moscow]] in 1948. She earned a master's degree in physics from [[Moscow State University]] in 1953, and completed her doctoral studies there in 1960; her dissertation research, "On the stability of self-oscillatory systems and automatic control systems in the presence of random influences", was written under advisor Sergei Pavlovich Strelkov.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Polina Landa |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=146261 |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> She defended a second dissertation, "Investigation of the dynamic and statistical characteristics of optical quantum generators and amplifiers", in 1972.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Rosenblum |first1=Michael |last2=McClintock |first2=Peter V. E. |date=2022-12-01 |title=In memoriam—Polina S. Landa (15 February 1931–21 October 2022) |journal=Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science |volume=32 |issue=12 |article-number=120401 |doi=10.1063/5.0136898 |bibcode=2022Chaos..32l0401R |issn=1054-1500|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Career==
Landa joined the faculty of [[Moscow State University]] in 1956, and remained there as a researcher and professor until she retired in 2020. She taught, did research on [[oscillation]]s, with applications in plasma, lasers, and acoustics, and supervised twelve doctoral students through to the completion of their degrees.<ref name=":0" /> She was a visiting researcher at [[Lancaster University]] in 1999 and 2003.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=August 1999 |title=Visitors to Lancaster |url=http://www1.maths.leeds.ac.uk/applied/news.dir/issue17.dir/news/acad.html#lanc |journal=UK Nonlinear News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=August 2003 |title=Lancaster Linear Group Visitors |url=http://www.amsta.leeds.ac.uk/applied/news.dir/issue33.dir/news/news.html#lancaster |journal=UK Nonlinear News}}</ref> She was a member of the Russian National Committee on Theoretical and Applied Mechanics.<ref name=":0" />

* ''Self-Oscillations in Systems with Finite Number of Degrees of Freedom'' (1980)
* ''Self-Oscillations in Distributed Systems'' (1983)
* ''Stochastic and Chaotic Oscillations'' (1987, with Yuri Neimark)<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Neimark |first1=Yurii Isaakovich |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nDXojK82iHwC |title=Stochastic and Chaotic Oscillations |last2=Landa |first2=Polina Solomonovna |date=1992 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-0-7923-1530-8 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Landa died in 2022, at the age of 91, in Moscow.<ref name=":0" />
